items.title: Workers - Workers Builds now posts preview URLs in seconds
items.content_text: Workers Builds now consistently posts preview URLs to GitHub pull requests and GitLab merge requests within a few seconds of a build completing, so you can start testing and reviewing your changes sooner. Previously, posting preview URLs could often take minutes. For details, refer to Workers Builds GitHub integration and Workers Builds GitLab integration .

The agents/models/opencode provider connects OpenCode to Workers AI through the AI binding. OpenCode plugins extend the harness with custom tools, remote MCP servers, and skills. When you give the web_search tool to your agent, the model provides a query and max results, and receives back a short numbered list of titles, URLs, and trimmed descriptions. items.title: Cloudflare One - Unified dashboard navigation for Zero Trust
items.content_text: The Cloudflare dashboard now combines Zero Trust and main dashboard navigation. You can move between Cloudflare products from the same navigation. All customers can browse Zero Trust products from the primary navigation. Zero Trust customers can also access other services from this navigation. These include the developer platform, account memberships, and resource tagging. As part of this change, the Zero Trust Network items were removed in favor of the new experiences available under Networking

items.title: Queues - Queues now supports EU, US, and FedRAMP jurisdictions
items.content_text: You can now create Cloudflare Queues with jurisdictional restrictions, ensuring that messages published to a queue are stored and processed only within a specific jurisdiction. This helps you comply with data residency requirements such as the GDPR ↗︎ or FedRAMP ↗︎ . To create a jurisdiction-restricted queue with the Cloudflare CLI ( cf ), use the --jurisdiction flag: cf queues create --queue-name my-eu-queue --jurisdiction eu You can also pass a jurisdiction parameter when calling the Create Qu

items.title: Workers - More time for requests to finish during Workers runtime updates
items.content_text: Pending requests and connections to Workers now have a grace period of up to 20 minutes during Workers runtime updates. Previously, the grace period was up to 30 seconds. This gives long-running HTTP requests, streamed AI responses, and live WebSocket sessions more time to continue before an update interrupts them. items.title: Agents - Cloudflare API MCP server serves Cloudflare skills
items.content_text: The Cloudflare API MCP server now serves Cloudflare skills ↗︎ through the Skills over MCP extension ↗︎ . MCP clients that support the extension discover the skills with skills/list and read their files at skill://<name>/<path> . To use them, add https://mcp.cloudflare.com/mcp to an MCP client that supports the extension ↗︎ .

items.content_text: We celebrated our 16th birthday with 46 announcements across open source, post-quantum security, AI agents, and developer platform upgrades. Here’s a day-by-day roundup of everything we shipped.

items.title: One year later: the power of 1.1.1.1 interns
items.content_text: A year after announcing our goal to hire 1,111 interns, more than 750 early-career builders have shipped real products across 48 teams at Cloudflare. From Birthday Week launches to post-quantum security, our interns prove that AI amplifies human potential instead of replacing it.

items.content_text: Cloudflare is launching eight major updates that bring logs, traces, analytics, alerts, dashboards, querying, and telemetry export into one observability platform, with simpler and more predictable pricing.

items.title: Streamline: custom video pipelines with Cloudflare Stream and Workers
items.content_text: Streamline demonstrates how to build long-running, continuous video processing pipelines by pairing Cloudflare Workers and Durable Objects with a containerized media engine.

items.title: Introducing Web Search API via AI Gateway
items.content_text: Cloudflare AI Gateway now supports native web search API integration in partnership with Ceramic.ai, Exa, and Linkup. Developers can now inject real-time web context into model inference calls via AI Gateway, REST APIs, or Workers bindings.

items.title: Introducing Cloudflare Traces: follow requests through our entire platform
items.content_text: Cloudflare Traces shows how a request moves through security rules, transformations, cache, routing, Workers, and your origin, then follows it across services running anywhere in your stack.

items.title: Updates on our pledge to make Cloudflare features accessible to everyone
items.content_text: A year after pledging to eliminate two-tier product access, Cloudflare has expanded Logpush, multi-account governance, and higher platform limits to all accounts. Here is an update on our progress, how we dogfood these tools internally, and what is coming next.

items.title: Announcing Cloudflare OHTTP Gateway – expanding access to Cloudflare’s privacy-preserving infrastructure
items.content_text: We’re announcing the closed beta of a self-serve Cloudflare OHTTP Gateway. We’re also renaming our Privacy Gateway to Cloudflare OHTTP Relay to better distinguish the two products.

items.title: Follow the thread: a new dashboard to investigate account abuse
items.content_text: Fraudsters are increasingly using AI to bypass stateless security checks. Cloudflare's new Account Abuse Protection dashboard uses stateful analysis and edge-generated Hashed User IDs to help teams investigate and block account abuse.

items.title: Protected Quick Tunnels: simple accountless authentication for your next dev project
items.content_text: Quick Tunnels now support email authentication. Add --allowed-mail to one cloudflared command, and only the addresses or domains you list can reach your local app. No Cloudflare account required on either side.

items.title: Building for good: How civil society organizations are automating on Cloudflare
items.content_text: Some of the world's leading organizations are building the future of non-profit work with Cloudflare.

items.title: 2026 Birthday week: network performance update
items.content_text: Cloudflare now ranks as the fastest provider across 74% of the top 1,000 global networks. By incorporating background telemetry from Cloudflare Challenge Pages, we have expanded our real-user measurement scale while maintaining user privacy.

items.title: Introducing Clef: our open-source decision models, and new RL fine-tuning platform
items.content_text: We are introducing Clef and Clef-flash, open-source decision models hosted on Workers AI for high-speed classification and agentic workflows. Also launching: a new reinforcement learning platform that allows developers to fine-tune decision models using their own data.

items.title: One year later: Sovereign AI and the fight for choice
items.content_text: AI sovereignty is not a zero-sum game, but many governments now believe it is. Cloudflare's answer: more local open-source models, model-agnostic security tools, and a commitment to giving nations genuine choice.

items.title: Introducing Workers KV Instant — powered by Quicksilver
items.content_text: Workers KV Instant delivers sub-2ms p99 read latencies and 250ms global replication across Cloudflare’s 300+ edge locations. KV Instant eliminates cold-read penalties and uses the familiar Workers KV API.

items.title: Cloudflare OS: your company’s agent workspace, managed for you
items.content_text: Cloudflare OS gives everyone in your organization an agent workspace that knows how your company works and connects to its data and systems. We’re opening the waitlist for fully managed deployments that you’ll be able to launch in a few clicks.

items.title: Announcing Cloudflare K2: serverless event streams
items.content_text: Cloudflare K2 is a serverless event streaming service built directly on top of R2 object storage for high-scale data movement and long-term retention. By decoupling producers and consumers at the edge, K2 enables durable, ordered log streams without the operational overhead of traditional broker clusters.

items.title: We want you to build the next Git platform on Cloudflare
items.content_text: Cloudflare is hosting a competition to see who will build the next Git platform for an era of AI agents. Artifacts is in open beta, with Workers bindings, data jurisdiction controls, and event subscriptions for repository changes.

items.title: AI Search is now generally available
items.content_text: AI Search is now generally available. It embeds image pixels directly for visual search, runs optical character recognition on scanned PDFs, accepts files up to 10 MiB, and works with any chat model. Here's what's new and how pricing works.

items.title: Support for modern cryptographic algorithms in Workers
items.content_text: Cloudflare Workers is adding opt-in support for post-quantum-resistant algorithms ML-KEM and ML-DSA. You can try it today.

items.title: Introducing Cloudflare Basin: an open, serverless data platform, now generally available
items.content_text: Cloudflare Basin is built on Apache Iceberg and R2 Object Storage. With general availability, developers can ingest, manage, and query large datasets at scale without paying data egress fees.

items.title: Cloudflare Impact reaches $100 million in donations
items.content_text: This week, Cloudflare's Impact programs will reach $100 million in donated services. This milestone means that thousands of entities including journalists, civil society, state and local governments, election management bodies, and public schools are being protected from cyberattacks.

items.title: Cut your AI spend with AI Gateway's Auto Router
items.content_text: Cloudflare AI Gateway now features a model router that evaluates request complexity using an edge-deployed classifier to select the optimal model. By balancing expected output quality against token costs, organizations can dramatically cut AI spend while maintaining performance.

items.title: Detect and send production issues straight to your agent
items.content_text: You can now use built-in error monitoring in Cloudflare Workers to group production failures and send stack traces, logs, traces, and application context directly to a coding agent to investigate further and open a pull request.

items.title: Simplifying domains for people and agents
items.content_text: Cloudflare Registrar’s new search delivers fast, transparent results across 420+ extensions using Workers, Durable Objects, and WebSockets. Its expanded API and cf CLI also let agents search, register, and transfer domains.

items.title: Monetization Gateway beta: charge AI agents for consumption with HTTP 402
items.content_text: Cloudflare’s AI Gateway, Ceramic.ai, Stocktwits, and more are using the Cloudflare Monetization Gateway today to charge agents for access to tokens, APIs, and MCP tools. U.S.-based sellers can now apply for access to the closed beta.

items.title: Pay Per Use: when AI uses your work, you should get paid
items.content_text: Pay Per Use is now in beta. AI companies report when they use publishers’ content, and Cloudflare handles billing, payouts, and reporting, so our customers are paid according to use.

items.title: Identify AI model overuse with User Insights
items.content_text: AI Gateway User Insights now adds task, model, turn, and user categories to help teams understand AI adoption and make better model decisions. This is available free to AI Gateway users.

items.title: Cloudflare Containers, rebuilt to scale agent sandboxes
items.content_text: Cloudflare Containers now start 6x faster, let your agent choose each sandbox's image and instance type at runtime, and support filesystem snapshots in public beta, all controlled from a Durable Object.

items.title: The Internet has a second audience
items.content_text: More than half the traffic reaching sites on Cloudflare is now automated, and AI agents are the fastest-growing part of it. We're giving site owners the tools to see who's visiting, decide who gets in, and charge for access.

items.title: Preventing quantum downgrade attacks against IPsec
items.content_text: A sophisticated attacker with a quantum computer can exploit a protocol design flaw to downgrade post-quantum IPsec tunnels to classical crypto. We helped the IETF develop a transcript authentication extension to prevent these attacks.
